pr_comments:
Looking at https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/22426 it looks like all problems in that issue were addressed.

Reading the diff, I have enough of a mental model to say that all changes look correct, but enough of a distance from merge that I should probably also check the code and run the changes.

You mention there's still room for improvement, what's your general testing strategy? Run through games and dig into the menu?

Basically I've come across the majority of the issues while trying to actually use the new feature. And most of the cosmetic changes hints (moving and renaming items, etc.) come from my family members as regular users. Then I found some more potential issues while trying to understand the code, so I did specific tests to confirm those (like rewriting of the manually created savestate).

When I say there's room for improvement, I can actually think of 2:
1. Regarding the [26e7167](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/22490/commits/26e71673dc5937cf31d5ba750a591d51dedee6dc):
I'm not sure what was the original author's intention here. Possibly update the current autosave upon opening the Saves menu? I think that this is actually not needed, because when you open this menu, you are probably about to Save or Load the game, so you don't need to update the current autosave, right? But if it is actually needed, then we would need to make sure that it only happens when the Autosave is actually enabled, otherwise there is no autosave to rewrite so a new savestate is created every time you open the menu. However, I don't know if there is an easy way to access the Autosave settings from that scope.

2. The second one is more about the design, regarding the [2cba454](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/22490/commits/2cba454855639c37b7a9d08b88f5c08e751e240f).

I'm sure that I don't like the former behavior:
- You create a savestate manually (let's say just before some important moment in the game).
- The other day you load the savestate and continue the game.
- You want to return back to the saved position, but the savestate is rewritten by the Autosave.

While the proposed solution is better, it still has its flaws:
- The other day you load from the manual savestate and continue.
- After 10 seconds a new autosave is created.
- You lose the battle, so you load from the original savestate again.
- After 10 seconds a new autosave is created.
- When you continue the "load and die" loop, you'll end up with several autosaves to delete.

IMHO it is better, but still not perfect. I'm not sure what would be the best solution for this. Maybe to find the latest autosave and continue to rewrite it when loading from the manual savestate?

You mention design. I think the issue is that we need to design a more intuitive UX, which is hard for a 10" interface.

I had the idea for a skewmorphism using the "library" paradigm not just for games but also for gameplay.

You can separate all savestate-capable gameplay into "chapters". Chapters could work well for separating gameplay, because like savestates they can be given an optional title, they have a timestamp and duration, and they can be sequenced. They can even be automatically numbered, unlike savestates which require intentional slotting.

Chapters are also a creative application of a video paradigm to games. Similar to how RetroPlayer was motivated by making games easier to play by treating them like videos.

How would you design a UX that is accessible to a media center novice just barely capable of chapter navigation?

Actually I'm happy with the way it looks now.

I'd probably try to improve it with 2 small features:
1. Visually differentiate between autosave and manual save (currently the user can't see it).
2. Improve the [2cba454](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/22490/commits/2cba454855639c37b7a9d08b88f5c08e751e240f) when loading the manual savestate to prevent creating the unlimited number of autosaves as described before.

Something like this:
- When loading manual savestate.
- Try to find newest autosave.
- If the autosave's time is newer than the time of the loaded manual savestate, then set the `m_autosavePath` to this autosave, so it is going to be rewritten instead of creating a new one.

I've done the ID re-ordering and I've added the label to autosaves (if there is no label set manually by the user). IMHO this will help the users to understand that there is a difference between the autosave and the manual save.

Also please note the following comment regarding the [b1e7233](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/22490/commits/b1e723327b0e7346595f004d19478cf3b6eae603):
1. When you start the game from the manual savestate, the _m_autosavePath_ is not set (is empty) and so the new autosave is created to save the progress as expected. The same happens when you start a new game.
2. But if you load the manual savestate using the in-game menu with Autosave enabled, then the _m_autosavePath_ was already set to the last autosave that you were using and it is not being reset here, so it continues to save progress to that autosave slot.

I like this behavior, I just wanted to explicitly mention it. Similar thing happens also when you reset the emulator with the Reset button from the in-game menu. It will continue to save progress to the same autosave slot as before the reset.

Overall I'm happy with this now. One last missing feature is to be able to rename and delete the savestates from the in-game menu, but that is beyond this PR.
@lrusak, can you change the label to _Component: Games_? Eventually please add the _Backport: Done_.

I did a round of test builds with this change if anyone needs a build: https://github.com/garbear/xbmc/releases/tag/retroplayer-20-20230121

General testing seems good.

I've tested the feature on Windows. It works well. The proliferation of autosaves is indeed a little annoying though.

![screenshot00001](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/531482/213953394-a586da35-5518-4f11-892c-16c547fbabcd.png)

> I've tested the feature on Windows. It works well. The proliferation of autosaves is indeed a little annoying though.

I've found out that it is actually not that bad when you start really using it (not just testing). The new autosave is created only when you start the game from the manual savestate. In the real life you only start the game once and then, if you need to go back to the manual save, you load it from the in-game menu. This way you only get one new autosave. You can even avoid new autosave completely by starting the game from existing autosave and then loading the manual save from the in-game menu as many times as needed, until you win the fight.

What I am missing in the real life though is the context menu in the in-game savestate manager, which would let me to **overwrite**, **rename** and **delete** savestates. I like the simple interface and the default actions as it is now, but for advanced users it would be nice to have more control from the in-game by context menu. Basically the **rename** and **delete** are already implemented in the start game menu (in the context menu as well), so adding the same ability to the in-game menu + adding the **overwrite**, which would get the label from the selected savestate, delete it and created a new one with the same label.

I have re-based the PR to clean the git log and I've added the translation for "Autosave" as requested by @garbear. The PR is now ready to be merged (at least from my part). @garbear how about you?

The backport is ready as well, changes are identical.

> I've found out that it is actually not that bad when you start really using it (not just testing).

Good point. I finally completed my Nexus Kodi setup. In my next retro sesh we'll get some real life family member and friend testing. Let's get these fixes in now and we can follow up with changes from future real-life testing.

> What I am missing in the real life though is the context menu in the in-game savestate manager

Agreed, this is a UX problem! Next time I'm hacking on Kodi I'll prioritize this change. Unless you want to take it on. GUI work is challenging but rewarding.
Windows builds seem to be failing from fallout of https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/pull/21248. Maybe rebase on master again and cross your fingers?

@garbear, I have updated the translation strings as requested.

issue_context.body:
<!--- Please fill out this template to the best of your ability. You can always edit this issue once you have created it. -->
<!--- Read the following link before you create a new problem report: https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:Submit_a_bug_report  -->
## Bug report
### Describe the bug
<!--- Provide a more detailed introduction to the issue itself, and why you consider it to be a bug -->
<!--- A bug report that is not clear will be closed -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
While playing with the new Savestate manager in the Nexus I've found the following issues. Both issues happen when the Autosave feature is turned off in the Settings:

1. You cannot load a saved state. You can still create save states from the in-game menu and those are created correctly, but until you enable the Autosave feature the saved states loading is broken (probably a left over condition from before the Savestate manager).
**Steps to reproduce**
**a)** disable Autosave in the Settings
**b)** try to load a saved state
**c)** the emulator is started like a new clean instance

2. A new save state is created every time you open the in-game Saved games menu. This shouldn't happen when the Autosave is disabled. This seems to be a kind of opposite problem than the first one (missing condition).
**Steps to reproduce**
**a)** disable Autosave in the Settings
**b)** open the in-game Saved games menu
**c)** watch the growing number of save states (automatically created every time you open the menu)

3. This one is more of a suggestion than a real problem. The "Saved games" menu option doesn't fully reflect what it actually does. IMHO this is not a "saved game", it doesn't even have to be a game at all, it is a saved state of the whole emulator, so probably "Savestate manager" or simply "Savestates" would be a more appropriate name for the menu item.

4. Also the "New game" option in the Select savestate window should be simply "New" (without the game) for a better consistency.



### Your Environment
Used Operating system:
<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->
<!--- Put your text below this line. Checkboxes can easily be ticked once issue is created -->
 - [ ] Android
 - [ ] iOS
 - [ ] tvOS
 - [X] Linux
 - [ ] macOS
 - [ ] Windows
 - [ ] Windows UWP

 - Operating system version/name: LibreELEC 11
 - Kodi version: 20.0rc2



<!--- End of this issue -->
*note: Once the issue is made we require you to update it with new information or Kodi versions should that be required.
Team Kodi will consider your problem report however, we will not make any promises the problem will be solved.*
comments:
The first issue comes from here:
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/e9c08df8289b97e539b8b45540ad42de858fffae/xbmc/cores/RetroPlayer/RetroPlayer.cpp#L193

IMHO we should try to load the savestate if AutosaveEnabled() **OR** if the game client is being started from the new Select savestate window.

EDIT:
Here is my proposal, but I haven't tested it so it is just an idea:

1. Remove the _bRestoreState_ parameter from _CRetroPlayer::CreatePlayback()_ completely.
2. And replace the check for _bRestoreState_ here:
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/e9c08df8289b97e539b8b45540ad42de858fffae/xbmc/cores/RetroPlayer/RetroPlayer.cpp#L609
Replace it with _if (!savestatePath.empty())_. Similar check is already being used when getting the game client from the selected savestate.

Less code seems always better. There is currently no need to check for enabled auto save feature at all, so we simply try to load the savestate if the savestatePath is set.
Also someone more familiar with the code please check this block:
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/e9c08df8289b97e539b8b45540ad42de858fffae/xbmc/cores/RetroPlayer/RetroPlayer.cpp#L155

I believe that the whole block can be safely removed (including the referenced strings) because there is currently no longer a way to trigger this. It was useful before the Savestate manager when you could have started the game with the Autosave enabled but you manually select a different game client. It is no longer possible as the game client is now determined automatically from the savestate itself.
Here is another thing to consider:
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/7b8df883185bb8d13d099931ff6a286c13d3a499/xbmc/cores/RetroPlayer/playback/ReversiblePlayback.cpp#L227

I'm not sure if I understand the code well, but do we want to set _m_autosavePath_ unconditionally here? IMHO when you load the manually created savestate, then you don't want the Autosave feature to rewrite it subsequently. Instead you probably want to keep this manually created savestate intact and the Autosave should use a new slot instead of updating the one you've loaded from.

So my proposal would be to set _m_autosavePath_ here conditionally only if _savestate->Type()_ is _SAVE_TYPE::AUTO_.

This one affects the behavior with Autosave turned on.
And here is the source of the second issue from the OP:
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/7bfc3183739042b1f3cd1904a0e4c12eb7ded096/xbmc/games/dialogs/osd/DialogInGameSaves.cpp#L57

My proposal is to call this one conditionally only if Autosave is enabled in settings:
```
if (m_gameServices.GameSettings().AutosaveEnabled()) {
	gameSettings->CreateSavestate(true);
}
```

review_comments: If I am not wrong there is no other way to save the progress, so if you have loaded a manual save state the progress will never be saved. The only way to save will be to create a new save state

I think that the _CreateSavestate(true)_ is called no matter if _m_autosavePath_ is set, so it should work the same way as when you start completely new game and it should create a new autosave in a new slot.

It comes here:
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/26e71673dc5937cf31d5ba750a591d51dedee6dc/xbmc/cores/RetroPlayer/playback/ReversiblePlayback.cpp#L184

So the _savePath_ is set empty from the empty _m_autosavePath_.
And then in the _AddSavestate()_ the empty _savePath_ is handled and it creates a new savestate.
Then the _m_autosavePath_ is set back from the _savePath_, so subsequent autosaves are saved to the same slot.

EDIT: The empty _savestatePath_ is handled here:
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/92130d45f985fb111fdfb2bdbfbb70eb72bf3dcf/xbmc/cores/RetroPlayer/savestates/SavestateDatabase.cpp#L49

Also I believe that I've tested this specific behavior, but I'll double check this again tomorrow to be sure.

The bad thing about this is that for every load from a manual savestate you'll get new autosave slot created, so when you load a lot you'll need to delete the bunch of autosaves. I believe it is still better than having your manual savestate rewritten by autosave.

So, I've tested it again and it does what was expected (all tests with Autosave feature enabled):
1. When loading from autosave: It rewrites the original autosave every 10 seconds or on exit.
2. If you load from a manual savestate: It will create a new autosave slot after 10 seconds or upon exit.

My only complaint here from the user's perspective is that I don't know whether I am loading a manual savestate or an autosave. How about at least adding caption "Autosave" to autosaves for now?
The savestate object has a `Type()` method that can tell if it's an autosave. Should we use that?
